Subject: LumosAI POC: scope, success criteria & capacity plan

Hi Samantha / James —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the PoC moving (TL;DR at bottom):

Recap from call:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Inference for low-latency document QA across LumosAI's 40M-document knowledge base (initial scope: 10M docs).
- Success criteria proposed by Lumos: 95th percentile latency < 400ms for single-chat queries, semantic search recall >= 0.78 vs baseline, and steady-state token cost below their internal target (TBD).
- Timeline: 4-week evaluation window with a 2-week prep/onboarding period.

Open / action items we discussed:
1) Define exact evaluation prompt set and baseline metrics (you offered to share a sample set).
2) Confirm compute baseline and burst expectations so we can reserve capacity.
3) Sign MSA / trial addendum (procurement loop) — I can share standard language but will work with Grace on capacity terms.
4) Schedule a technical kickoff with Solutions Eng (Grace) next week.

Capacity asks (proposed):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) for the trial window. This covers steady load and allows warm KV cache for most session traffic.
- Burst policy: Autoscale up to 12 GPU-equivalents (i.e., up to 3x baseline) for short bursts (up to 2 hours/day total), with manual approval for sustained bursts beyond that.
- Prewarming: We'll prewarm models for the first 4 hours of the trial to avoid cold-start latencies.

Attachments: I attached the PoC requirements spreadsheet and our PoC capacity playbook for reference.

Next steps (my ask):
- Samantha: share the evaluation prompt set + expected concurrency profile (QPS peaks, typical session length).
- James / procurement: loop procurement contact for contract review (we can use a short addendum for reserved capacity).
- Grace: can you confirm technical owners and availability for a kickoff next Wed/Thu?

TL;DR: We propose a 4-week PoC, baseline reserve 4x A100-equivalents, burst to 12 for short windows, sample eval prompts and procurement contact needed to lock dates.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if that helps.

Cheers,

Thanks Rishi — great notes and exactly what we needed. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with the team:

Success criteria updates:
- Latency: target 95th <= 350ms for single-document retrieval + model call for standard prompts (we can be flexible by 50ms).
- Quality: semantic search recall >= 0.80 (we'll provide labeled queries).
- Cost: our finance team wants a rough estimate of token cost per 1k requests for the baseline config before we sign.

Workload profile (initial):
- Typical QPS: 15–25 during business hours (peak 40 for short windows).
- Average session length: 6–12 turns; average generated tokens per turn ~60.

Compute ask:
- 4 x A100 baseline sounds reasonable; can you confirm how cold-starts look for the 10M doc index and whether we should expect more GPUs?
- For burst: we need to allow up to 3x baseline for short events (marketing load tests) but would like to cap cost: please include an estimate of incremental cost for 1-hour and 4-hour bursts.

Procurement: Looping procurement@lumosai.com separately — they requested any standard addendum and a DocuSign link if possible.

I'll upload the labeled query set by EOD tomorrow. Also happy to meet next Wed 10–11 PT for the technical kickoff.

Great — thanks for the fast turnaround, Samantha. Short answers inline:

- Cold starts / 10M doc index: with our prefix KV cache and prewarming strategy, cold-start penalty is usually ~600–900ms for first few requests if the model weights are cold, but once warmed (we'll prewarm for 4h) you should see the ~300–350ms 95th percentile. The index size is within normal bounds; the main variable is model size and context window.

- Burst cost estimates (very rough initial numbers):
  - Baseline (4x A100-equivalent, steady 8–12 QPS): ~$1,200/day token + infra amortization (placeholder).
  - 1-hour burst to 12 GPUs (3x baseline): incremental infra cost ~ $180–$300 (depending on region).
  - 4-hour burst: incremental infra cost ~ $720–$1,200.
These are rule-of-thumb; Grace will follow up with more precise rate cards and region pricing.

- DocuSign / procurement: I will send the trial addendum and DocuSign link to procurement@lumosai.com after we confirm the exact reserved numbers.

Technical kickoff: Wed 10–11 PT works — Grace, can you confirm?

I'll also attach a short one-pager with our PoC runbook highlights.

Thanks — Rishi

Hi all — thanks for scheduling the kickoff. A few technical clarifications and the capacity playbook summary for the PoC:

Recommended PoC configuration (initial):
- Model: Llama-2-70B-v0.3 quantized FP16 (or your preference) — we'll provide both FP16 and INT8 variants for comparison.
- Baseline reserved compute: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent (dedicated). This will give you stable KV cache behavior and consistent latency.
- Autoscaling policy: scale by node increments of 2 GPUs, up to a hard cap of 12 GPUs. Scale triggers: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 60% for 90s OR queue latency > 200ms for 120s.
- Burst policy: automatic for up to 2 hours/day (no manual approval for short bursts); beyond that require manual approval from the Lumos account team.
- Prewarm window: 4 hours before the start of peak testing windows (we can coordinate via the kickoff calendar).

Observability & gates:
- We'll instrument per-route 95/99 latency, per-request token counts, and a quality evaluation hook (we'll run batch evals nightly over the labeled set you provide).
- Acceptance gates: 95th latency <= 350ms and recall >= 0.80 for 7 consecutive days within the 4-week window. If gates not met, we'll run a joint troubleshooting sprint and recommend mitigations (model variant, quantization, or increased baseline).

Operational notes:
- Warm pools: we keep a 1-GPU warm pool to speed up additional node attach; prewarming will fill that pool.
- KV cache sizing: for 10M docs we recommend a 200GB KV cache initially — Grace will confirm exact sizing after we ingest a sample.

Attachments: PoC capacity playbook (PDF) and the Lumos requirements sheet (you shared) are attached here too.

Action items assigned:
- Lumos (Samantha): upload labeled query set (Samantha — EOD 2026-12-13 expected).
- Redwood (Grace): finalize estimated incremental cost per burst length and confirm KV cache sizing after sample ingest (ETA: 24–48h).
- Redwood (Rishi): send procurement DocuSign and standard trial addendum once baseline numbers are confirmed.

I'll be on the kickoff Wed 2026-12-15 10:00–11:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

Cheers,
